title: Extractability
content: Extractability describes how well a passage retains its meaning when read separately from the surrounding page.

meta.why: A definition or instruction is easier to reuse accurately when it names its subject and keeps its conditions, such as cutoffs or exclusions, in the same passage.
meta.example: “Orders placed by noon ship the same business day” is clearer on its own than “They go out then,” and both versions still need any relevant exclusions.
meta.check: Read a section’s opening without its heading, then make sure the opening names the subject and keeps important qualifications beside the claim.
meta.limitation: We use extractability as an editorial check, and no engine publishes a score for it or promises a citation for passing it. Cutting a passage too short can also strip out context the reader needs.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: optimizing for generative AI | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide | Platform documentation
